strings.group.help: Digital and analog pin access. <pin> accepts 4, 0-5 or 1,4,8-10
strings.need_two_pins: Need at least two testable pins; got %d
strings.pin_absent: GPIO %d does not exist on this chip
strings.pin_input_only: GPIO %d is input-only on this chip
strings.pin_not_adc: GPIO %d is not an ADC-capable pin
strings.rc.help: Measure each net's pull-up strength and capacitance
strings.rc_absent: %4d   does not exist on this chip
strings.rc_header: pin    external   with int    pull-up      net C
strings.rc_intro: Pull-up strength and net capacitance. Nothing else may be driving these pins.
strings.rc_ref_absent: Reference GPIO %d does not exist on this chip
strings.rc_ref_not_pulled_up: GPIO %d does not behave like a pulled-up net, so it cannot be the reference
strings.rc_ref_too_fast: GPIO %d rises too fast to time, so it cannot be the reference. Use a weaker pull-up
strings.rc_reference_assumed:
Internal pull-up assumed to be %.0fk, so absolute values are good to a factor
of two and ratios between pins are exact. 'ref <pin> <kohms>' measures it.
strings.rc_reference_measured: Internal pull-up measured as %.1fk against the %s reference on GPIO %s
strings.read.help: Read the logic level of pin(s)
strings.short.help: Find pins shorted together, adjacent pairs first
strings.short_adjacent_header: Adjacent pins (where a solder bridge usually lands):
strings.short_held_low_header: Held low whatever is driven, so not testable and not a short:
strings.short_held_low_note: A grounded net, a card-detect switch or an output driving low.
strings.short_no_adjacent: no consecutively numbered pins in the set
strings.short_scan_intro:
Short scan across %d pins. Each is driven low in turn, so do not run this
on a bus another device may be driving.
strings.skip_absent: Skipping GPIO %d: does not exist on this chip
strings.skip_duplicate: Skipping GPIO %d: listed more than once
strings.state_invalid: Invalid state '%s'. Use true/false, 1/0 or high/low
strings.survey.help: Census every pin: pull-ups, driven lines, and what they suggest
strings.survey_capacitance_note: Capacitance separates a bare pad from a routed net and nothing more; a clock or data line is driven, not pulled, and looks like any other idle input from here.
strings.survey_held_summary: %d pin%s held low by something driving an output; worth identifying before assuming a pin is free.
strings.survey_i2c_pair: GPIO %d and %d are the only pins with a deliberate pull-up, which is what an I2C bus looks like. Try:
strings.survey_i2c_try_swapped: i2c bus %d %d   (SCL and SDA the other way round)
strings.survey_intro: Surveying %d pins. Nothing else may be driving them.
strings.survey_many_pullups: More than a pair, so this may be several buses, or a reset or interrupt line. 'i2c scan' each likely pair.
strings.survey_no_pullups: No pin carries a bus-strength pull-up, so there is probably no I2C device wired to this board.
strings.survey_one_pullup: GPIO %d alone has a pull-up, so more likely a reset, interrupt or enable line than a bus.
strings.survey_skipped_summary: %d pin%s skipped as unsafe to drive; the reason is on each row.
strings.why_absent: does not exist on this chip
strings.why_reserved: reserved for flash, PSRAM or a peripheral in use
